[[if test="is(ix=1)"]]A delivery van loses \({@r@}\%\) of its value every year; each year's loss is \({@r@}\%\) of its value at the start of that year. {@nm@} says: After \({@n@}\) years it has lost \({@nr@}\%\) of its value.[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=2)"]]A plot gains \({@r@}\%\) in value every year, on its value at the start of that year. {@nm@} says: After \({@n@}\) years it has gained \({@nr@}\%\) in value.[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=3)"]]A school computer loses \({@r@}\%\) of its value every year; each year's loss is \({@r@}\%\) of its value at the start of that year. {@nm@} says: After \({@n@}\) years it has lost \({@nr@}\%\) of its value.[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=4)"]]A plot gains \({@r@}\%\) in value every year, on its value at the start of that year. {@nm@} says: After \({@n@}\) years it has gained \({@nr@}\%\) in value.[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=5)"]]A water pump loses \({@r@}\%\) of its value every year; each year's loss is \({@r@}\%\) of its value at the start of that year. {@nm@} says: After \({@n@}\) years it has lost \({@nr@}\%\) of its value.[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=6)"]]A plot gains \({@r@}\%\) in value every year, on its value at the start of that year. {@nm@} says: After \({@n@}\) years it has gained \({@nr@}\%\) in value.[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=7)"]]A boda boda motorbike loses \({@r@}\%\) of its value every year; each year's loss is \({@r@}\%\) of its value at the start of that year. {@nm@} says: After \({@n@}\) years it has lost \({@nr@}\%\) of its value.[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=8)"]]A plot gains \({@r@}\%\) in value every year, on its value at the start of that year. {@nm@} says: After \({@n@}\) years it has gained \({@nr@}\%\) in value.[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=9)"]]A television loses \({@r@}\%\) of its value every year; each year's loss is \({@r@}\%\) of its value at the start of that year. {@nm@} says: After \({@n@}\) years it has lost \({@nr@}\%\) of its value.[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=10)"]]A plot gains \({@r@}\%\) in value every year, on its value at the start of that year. {@nm@} says: After \({@n@}\) years it has gained \({@nr@}\%\) in value.[[/if]]

(a) Which statement is right?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Find the actual percentage [[if test="dp"]]lost[[else]]gained[[/if]] over the \({@n@}\) years, correct to 1 decimal place.

[[input:ans2]] % [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Each year the value is multiplied by \({@dd(mone)@}\), so after \({@n@}\) years it is multiplied by \({@dd(mone)@}^{ {@n@} } = {@dispdp(float(mult),4)@}\), whatever the price.

[[if test="dp"]]

The value is \({@dispdp(float(remv),2)@}\%\) of the price, so it has lost \(100\% - {@dispdp(float(remv),2)@}\% = {@dispdp(float(pc),2)@}\% [[if test="integerp(10*pc)"]]=[[else]]\approx[[/if]] {@dispdp(float(floor(10*pc+1/2)/10),1)@}\%\): less than \({@nr@}\%\). Each year's \({@r@}\%\) is taken from a smaller value, so the losses shrink.

[[else]]

The value is \({@dispdp(float(remv),2)@}\%\) of the price, so it has gained \({@dispdp(float(remv),2)@}\% - 100\% = {@dispdp(float(pc),2)@}\% [[if test="integerp(10*pc)"]]=[[else]]\approx[[/if]] {@dispdp(float(floor(10*pc+1/2)/10),1)@}\%\): more than \({@nr@}\%\). Each year's \({@r@}\%\) is worked on a bigger value, so the gains grow.

[[/if]]

So {@nm@} is wrong: percentages for successive years do not add.

questiondescription.text:
Commercial Arithmetic III: adding yearly percentages

Grade 12 CBE Essential 2.4 (c): Judge a claim that yearly percentage changes add up, for appreciation and depreciation, and find the actual total percentage change.

Essential

This question is adapted from the revision exercise on page 139, question 3 of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 3 (Metric), ed. A. G. Howson, Cambridge University Press, 1967: comparing a value after several years of the same percentage change with the sum of the yearly rates; a claim to judge, appreciation and depreciation, new rates and years.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: Each year's \({@r@}\%\) is worked out on a different value, so the percentages do not just add. Try it with a price of Ksh \(100\).
The price does not matter: every price is multiplied by \({@dispdp(float(mult),4)@}\).

falsefeedback.text: Compare the multiplier \({@dd(mone)@}^{ {@n@} } = {@dispdp(float(mult),4)@}\) with \(1 [[if test="dp"]]-[[else]]+[[/if]] \frac{ {@nr@} }{100} = {@dd(1+(if dp then -nr else nr)/100)@}\).

truefeedback.text: That is the claim. Use the multiplier for \({@n@}\) years.
That is the value as a percentage of the price. [[if test="dp"]]Take it from \(100\%\).[[else]]Subtract \(100\%\).[[/if]]
